steps.note: Sync function: on insert, fill whichever of amount/total is missing from the other; on update, copy the changed one to the other.
steps.sql: CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION orders_sync_total() RETURNS trigger LANGUAGE plpgsql AS $f$ BEGIN IF TG_OP = 'INSERT' THEN IF NEW.total IS NULL THEN NEW.total := NEW.amount; ELSIF NEW.amount IS NULL THEN NEW.amount := NEW.total; END IF; ELSE IF NEW.amount IS DISTINCT FROM OLD.amount AND NEW.total IS NOT DISTINCT FROM OLD.total THEN NEW.total := NEW.amount; ELSIF NEW.total IS DISTINCT FROM OLD.total AND NEW.amount IS NOT DISTINCT FROM OLD.amount THEN NEW.amount := NEW.total; END IF; END IF; RETURN NEW; END $f$;

steps.note: Add nullable total (metadata-only, no rewrite) and the sync trigger in one transaction, so no row is ever inserted without total. Short lock_timeout with retries so app queries never queue behind the ACCESS EXCLUSIVE lock.
steps.sql: DO $$ DECLARE n int := 0; BEGIN LOOP BEGIN PERFORM set_config('lock_timeout', '200ms', true); ALTER TABLE orders ADD COLUMN total numeric(10,2); CREATE TRIGGER orders_sync_total BEFORE INSERT OR UPDATE ON orders FOR EACH ROW EXECUTE FUNCTION orders_sync_total(); EXIT; EXCEPTION WHEN lock_not_available THEN n := n + 1; IF n >= 100 THEN RAISE; END IF; PERFORM pg_sleep(0.3); END; END LOOP; END $$;

steps.note: Backfill procedure: copies amount to total in 50,000-row id ranges, committing after each batch (short row locks, no long transaction). Every row above the max id it sees was inserted with the trigger in place.
steps.sql: CREATE OR REPLACE PROCEDURE orders_backfill_total() LANGUAGE plpgsql AS $p$ DECLARE lo bigint := 0; hi bigint; BEGIN SELECT max(id) INTO hi FROM orders; WHILE lo < hi LOOP UPDATE orders SET total = amount WHERE id > lo AND id <= lo + 50000 AND total IS NULL; COMMIT; lo := lo + 50000; END LOOP; END $p$;

steps.note: Run the backfill (on its own so the procedure can COMMIT between batches).
Clean up the dead tuples from the backfill (plain VACUUM does not block reads or writes).
NOT NULL without a long lock, part 1: add CHECK (total IS NOT NULL) NOT VALID (instant, retried on lock timeout).
steps.sql: DO $$ DECLARE n int := 0; BEGIN LOOP BEGIN PERFORM set_config('lock_timeout', '200ms', true); ALTER TABLE orders ADD CONSTRAINT orders_total_not_null CHECK (total IS NOT NULL) NOT VALID; EXIT; EXCEPTION WHEN lock_not_available THEN n := n + 1; IF n >= 100 THEN RAISE; END IF; PERFORM pg_sleep(0.3); END; END LOOP; END $$;

steps.note: Part 2: validate the check. Full scan under SHARE UPDATE EXCLUSIVE, so reads and writes keep going. Fails (and stops the plan, in a safe state) if any row still lacks total.
steps.sql: ALTER TABLE orders VALIDATE CONSTRAINT orders_total_not_null;

steps.note: Part 3: SET NOT NULL uses the validated check and skips the scan; then drop the now-redundant check. Retried on lock timeout.
steps.sql: DO $$ DECLARE n int := 0; BEGIN LOOP BEGIN PERFORM set_config('lock_timeout', '200ms', true); ALTER TABLE orders ALTER COLUMN total SET NOT NULL; ALTER TABLE orders DROP CONSTRAINT orders_total_not_null; EXIT; EXCEPTION WHEN lock_not_available THEN n := n + 1; IF n >= 100 THEN RAISE; END IF; PERFORM pg_sleep(0.3); END; END LOOP; END $$;

steps.note: Switch the app to total. During the rolling update, old pods write amount and new pods write total; the trigger fills in the other column either way, and every row already has both.
Let terminating old pods finish draining (3 s shutdown delay plus in-flight requests) before amount goes away.
Safety check: stop here if any other session is still running a query that mentions amount.
steps.sql: DO $$ BEGIN IF EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM pg_stat_activity WHERE datname = current_database() AND pid <> pg_backend_pid() AND state = 'active' AND query ILIKE '%amount%') THEN RAISE EXCEPTION 'amount is still in use'; END IF; END $$;

steps.note: Contract: drop the trigger and the amount column in one transaction (retried on lock timeout), then the sync function.
steps.sql: DO $$ DECLARE n int := 0; BEGIN LOOP BEGIN PERFORM set_config('lock_timeout', '200ms', true); DROP TRIGGER orders_sync_total ON orders; ALTER TABLE orders DROP COLUMN amount; EXIT; EXCEPTION WHEN lock_not_available THEN n := n + 1; IF n >= 100 THEN RAISE; END IF; PERFORM pg_sleep(0.3); END; END LOOP; END $$; DROP FUNCTION orders_sync_total();

steps.note: Verify the end state: total is numeric(10,2) NOT NULL and amount is gone.
steps.sql: DO $$ BEGIN IF NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM information_schema.columns WHERE table_schema = 'public' AND table_name = 'orders' AND column_name = 'total' AND data_type = 'numeric' AND numeric_precision = 10 AND numeric_scale = 2 AND is_nullable = 'NO') THEN RAISE EXCEPTION 'total is not numeric(10,2) NOT NULL'; END IF; IF EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM information_schema.columns WHERE table_schema = 'public' AND table_name = 'orders' AND column_name = 'amount') THEN RAISE EXCEPTION 'amount still exists'; END IF; END $$;
